### Black & White — the Image > Adjustments command, not a Tools panel Tool

`color`

Photoshop's Black & White converts a color image to monochrome with six hue-sextant sliders, optionally tinted with a tone color.

Black & White is not a desaturation — it is a weighted mix, and the six sliders are the weights. Each of the six sextants of the color wheel, Reds, Yellows, Greens, Cyans, Blues and Magentas, gets its own control over how bright that family of hues becomes in the result, so a landscape can have a dark sky and a bright sky in the same conversion, and skin can be lifted without touching the greens. Every slider starts at a value that reproduces a conventional conversion — Photoshop opens the adjustment having already applied "a default grayscale conversion to your image" — and dragging one away from that value is the whole technique. Ticking Tint lays a uniform tone color over the monochrome so it reads as toned rather than neutral, which is how a sepia or a split-tone is made from a color original without going back to it.

| Reset                    | The reset icon that returns the sliders to their default values, and more generally the panel control that returns the adjustment to its original settings. THIS APP DIVERGES: Reset button resets Grayscale/Sepia/Saturation, not Black & White sextant sliders. Disabled unless uncommitted preview is live; restores panel's own defaults rather than sextant defaults.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `partial` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Colors/Color.tsx:185` |

**Shortcuts**

- `Shift+Cmd+Opt+B` — Open the Black & White command. Printed by Adobe's shipped shortcut sheet as "Black & White... Opt+Shift+Cmd+B" on macOS, and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+B on Windows; the app binds no shortcut for it.

**In this app:** `partial` — FUNDAMENTAL MISMATCH: Black & White is an Image > Adjustments command, or an adjustment layer — not a toolbar tool — so it has no rail entry, and the app reaches the same three CSS filters from Image > Adjustments > Desaturate, which is the Adobe command the bar's grayscale slider actually computes. That name is a bounded divergence rather than a match: sepia and saturation are controls Desaturate does not have. Adobe's Photo Filter is a separate command in the same submenu and it is a disabled item, because it is a lens filter with a Density slider and a Preserve Luminosity option and this bar reproduces none of those. No control of Photoshop's seven is reproduced, and the three sliders that are rendered are not Black & White controls: there is no sextant weighting anywhere in the app, so no per-hue decision can be made and the conversion is a flat luminance desaturation rather than a mix. The one control whose name the app shares is Reset, and it does not behave as Photoshop's does: it is disabled unless an uncommitted preview is live, and it restores that panel's own defaults rather than the sextant defaults, so a committed conversion can only be undone. The grayscale slider is the nearest thing to the whole panel and it is the one control that cannot stand in for it, because a hue-weighted mix and a luminance average differ the moment any of the six families is pushed. Sepia is not the Tint checkbox either: Tint lays a uniform tone color over a conversion whose mix you still control, and applying sepia is a second filter stage that tints the whole image rather than replacing its channel weights, so the two can be combined and the result is not the same look. Saturation belongs to no part of Black & White; it is a Hue/Saturation control, and the fact that this app has one is a leftover from the identity question this tool's shape was chosen to answer. Presets, Auto, Tint, Tint Color, the on-image adjustment icon and the six sliders are all absent. As with Levels, the engine is CSS filters (grayscale, sepia, saturate) not a per-hue mixer.

## Eyedropper and draw

Long-form research, provenance and unverified claims: [`src/tools/descriptions/eyedropper-draw.notes.md`](../src/tools/descriptions/eyedropper-draw.notes.md).

### Eyedropper Tool

`eyedropper` · **I**

Samples a color from the composited canvas at the pointer position and writes it to the foreground or background swatch; no drag preview, no history entry.

The Eyedropper reads a color from the composited workspace canvas and sets it as the foreground color (click) or background color (Alt-click). The sampled color is not added to the Swatches panel in this app. Sample Size sets the averaging footprint: Point Sample reads the exact center pixel, and 3×3 through 101×101 Average read the arithmetic mean of an odd-sided square clipped at the document frame. Adobe documents a drag gesture where the color box updates live; this app samples only on pointer-down, so a drag uses the first pixel, not the release pixel. Holding Alt from any painting tool temporarily activates the Eyedropper at its current Sample Size, sampling to the foreground color.

**Options bar**

| Control     | Photoshop                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | In this app                                                             |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sample Size | Sets the sampling footprint. Adobe enumerates seven entries: Point Sample (1×1), 3 by 3 Average, 5 by 5 Average, 11 by 11 Average, 31 by 31 Average, 51 by 51 Average, 101 by 101 Average. No Median entries. The menu order and labels match Adobe. The app seeds Point Sample. The footprint is an odd-sided square centred on the click, clipped at the document frame rather than shifted inward, reduced by an arithmetic mean with per-channel rounding.                                                                                                                                               | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Eyedropper/Eyedropper.tsx:22` |
| Sample      | Chooses which layers a sample is read from: All Layers, Current Layer, Current & Below, and the No Adjustments variants. Adobe enumerates that menu and states no default. Earlier versions expressed this as a Sample All Layers checkbox. The app renders no control for it. The `sampleAllLayers` field persists in settings (seeded `false` at `src/tools/settings.ts:265`), no control writes it, and a click that finds it `true` refuses loudly with `eyedropper-sample-all-layers-unsupported` rather than silently sampling the composite. The tool always samples the composited workspace canvas. | `missing`                                                               |

**Modifiers**

- **Alt** — Sets the sampled color as the background color instead of the foreground color. This is a click-only modifier in this app — there is no drag preview, so the sample is taken at pointer-down and the background swatch updates once.

**Shortcuts**

- `I` — Selects the Eyedropper. Holding I temporarily switches to it (spring-loaded) while another tool is active.
- `Shift+I` — Cycles the tools that share the letter: Eyedropper, Color Sampler, Ruler, Note and Count. The app cycles its three implemented members (Eyedropper, Color Sampler and Ruler); Note and Count are absent.

**In this app:** `partial` — The app implements the tool without a processor: it is a member of `PIXEL_FREE_TOOLS`, so it rasterizes nothing, has no `commit` kind, and its `toolsMap` entry carries only an icon and an options bar. A click dispatches `SET_COLOR` or `SET_BACKGROUND_COLOR` and nothing else — no history entry, not undoable (same class as zoom, panel move, tool switch). Three behaviors diverge from Photoshop: (1) Drag gesture: the app only has `handlePointerDown` wired to `onPointerDown`; no `onPointerMove` or `onPointerUp` handlers exist, so the sample is taken at pointer-down alone, no live preview during drag, and a drag samples the first pixel not the release pixel. (2) Sample All Layers: no control rendered; the `sampleAllLayers` field persists in settings but no control writes it, and `true` triggers a loud refusal (`eyedropper-sample-all-layers-unsupported`). (3) Swatches panel: the sampled color is not added to any swatches panel (the app has no Swatches panel). The composited read samples the workspace canvas (all visible layers composited), not the active layer alone. Alpha is dropped because the foreground/background swatches are `<input type="color">` which cannot express alpha. A click outside the frame dispatches nothing.

### Color Sampler Tool

`color-sampler`

Places up to four numbered markers with RGB/hex readouts. Drag to move; Alt-click or drag off-canvas to delete. Clear removes all markers.

The Color Sampler places persistent markers that report color values at fixed document locations. Up to four markers can exist simultaneously (Adobe documents four; some third-party observations say ten — the conflict is recorded in `src/tools/colorSampler.ts`). Click places a marker; dragging a marker moves it; dragging a marker outside the document frame deletes it; Alt-clicking a marker deletes it (the scissors cursor is not drawn — the app has no cursor registry). The Clear button removes all markers at once and is disabled when none exist. Sample Size sets the averaging footprint identically to the Eyedropper. The `Sample` dropdown (All Layers / Current Layer / Current & Below / No Adjustments variants) is not rendered; the app always reads the composited canvas. The `Change the display of the sample values` color-space switcher is not rendered (the app has no Info panel). Markers persist in a module store (`color-sampler-store.ts`), not in `StoreContext`, because a measurement is not a document fact. Readouts are frozen at placement — they do not track edits — because the app has no invalidation seam for pixel changes; a live readout would go stale on every edit. Readouts report RGB channels and hex only; no Lab, XYZ, or CMYK conversion exists.

**Options bar**

| Control                                 | Photoshop                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | In this app                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sample Size                             | Sets the footprint each marker reads, identical to the Eyedropper: Point Sample (1×1), 3 by 3 Average, 5 by 5 Average, 11 by 11 Average, 31 by 31 Average, 51 by 51 Average, 101 by 101 Average. The app renders all seven with Adobe labels and seeds Point Sample. The block is clipped at the frame edge rather than shifted inward. | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/ColorSampler/ColorSampler.tsx:64`  |
| Clear                                   | Removes every sampler at once. The button is disabled while no sampler exists. Implemented in `ColorSamplerToolArea` via `removeColorSampler` on the store.                                                                                                                                                                             | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/ColorSampler/ColorSampler.tsx:108` |
| Sample                                  | Photoshop's layer-source dropdown — All Layers, Current Layer, Current & Below and the No Adjustments variants. The app renders no control for it and reads the composited canvas for every marker (the Eyedropper's `All Layers` end). Recorded rather than omitted so the gap is visible.                                             | `missing`                                                                    |
| Change the display of the sample values | The per-marker colour-space switcher. Adobe documents its function in the Info panel; no source for the options-bar label itself. The app has no Info panel, so it renders no switcher and reports RGB and hex only, both direct readings of the sampled pixel.                                                                         | `missing`                                                                    |

**Modifiers**

- **Alt** — Deletes the marker under the pointer. The scissors cursor is not drawn (the app has no cursor registry), but the gesture is implemented. Checked on pointer-down before drag so a deletion takes precedence over a move.
- **Shift** — With the Eyedropper selected, Shift-click places a sampler and Shift+Alt-click deletes one. Both gestures live in `EyedropperToolArea` because `ColorSamplerToolArea` is not mounted while the Eyedropper holds the tile.

**Shortcuts**

- `I` — Selects Eyedropper if no member of the Eyedropper/Color Sampler/Ruler group is selected; otherwise keeps the current group member.
- `Shift+I` — Cycles the tools that share the letter: Eyedropper, Color Sampler, Ruler, Note and Count. The app cycles its three implemented members (Eyedropper, Color Sampler and Ruler); Note and Count are absent.

**In this app:** `partial` — The tool is a pixel-free tool — it has no entry in `toolProcessors.ts` and dispatches nothing. Adobe's one-line summary is a readout ("displays color values for up to four areas"), so placing a marker changes no pixel, creates no history state, and needs no durable operation. Six behaviors diverge from Photoshop: (1) Cap is four (Adobe docs say four; Julieanne Kost and two third-party observations say ten — recorded in `colorSampler.ts`). (2) Refusal at cap is loud, not a silent replacement — no source describes Photoshop replacing the oldest marker. (3) Readouts are RGB and hex only, frozen at placement (no Info panel, no invalidation seam). (4) `Sample` dropdown absent; always reads composite. (5) `Change display` absent; no color-space switcher. (6) Scissors cursor absent; no cursor registry. The marker glyph is a crosshair (drawn dark then light for contrast over any background); Adobe sources disagree on the glyph (crosshair vs target icon) and no Adobe sentence describes it. The hit radius for grab/delete is 8 document pixels (`COLOR_SAMPLER_HIT_RADIUS`), an app decision; Adobe states the gesture but publishes no tolerance. A document resize drops all samplers (`syncColorSamplerFrameSize`).

### Ruler Tool

`ruler`

Measures position, distance and angle with a nonprinting line; Shift constrains to 45°. Alt-drag an endpoint to add a protractor leg.

The Ruler measures distances and angles on the canvas without changing pixels. Drag a line from one point to another; the options bar reports the starting location (X, Y), horizontal and vertical distances (W, H), angle relative to the axis (A), and total length (D1). The line is a nonprinting overlay — it creates no history state, cannot be undone, and disappears when dragged out of the frame or cleared. Shift constrains the drag to 45° increments. Alt-drag (Option-drag on macOS) from within 8 document pixels of either endpoint pulls a second leg (D2) turning the measurement into a protractor; the angle (A) then reads the angle between the two legs. The double-click alternative ("double-click the line and drag") is not implemented because Adobe does not specify which end pivots. The measurement scale (Image > Analysis > Set Measurement Scale) is not implemented — the app has no Analysis menu. There is no Info panel; the options bar is the only surface for readouts. The ruler line survives a tool switch (Adobe: "If your document has an existing measuring line, selecting the Ruler tool causes it to be displayed").

**Options bar**

| Control               | Photoshop                                                                                                                                                                                                          | In this app                                                   |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| X, Y                  | The starting location of the measurement (the pointer-down point). The app reads the pointer-down point directly, so a drag that ends up and to the left of where it started reports the start it was given.       | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Ruler/Ruler.tsx:42` |
| W, H                  | The horizontal and vertical distances traveled from the x and y axes. Both are unsigned magnitudes in the app (a drag up-left reports the same W, H as down-right); Adobe prints them as unsigned distances too.   | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Ruler/Ruler.tsx:44` |
| A                     | The angle measured relative to the axis, in degrees. Exempt from document units per Adobe. With a protractor present, the bar re-reads A as the angle between the two legs (Adobe's own reuse of the same letter). | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Ruler/Ruler.tsx:46` |
| D1                    | The total length traveled, reported in document pixels (the app has no Units & Rulers preference). A measurement scale would rescale this number, not the geometry.                                                | `partial` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Ruler/Ruler.tsx:47` |
| D2                    | The second leg of a protractor. Present only after an Alt-drag has pulled a leg from an existing line; absent before that, not reported as zero.                                                                   | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Ruler/Ruler.tsx:50` |
| Clear                 | Removes the measuring line. Adobe describes two ways: drag it outside the image area, or press Clear. The app implements both; the button is disabled while no line exists.                                        | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Ruler/Ruler.tsx:64` |
| Use Measurement Scale | A checkbox Adobe's Ruler page does not document and this app does not render. The scale itself is an Image > Analysis menu command; the app has no Analysis submenu. Recorded so the gap is visible.               | `missing`                                                     |

**Modifiers**

- **Shift** — Constrains the measuring line to 45-degree increments — the drag is rotated onto the nearest multiple of 45° while keeping its length and direction of travel.
- **Alt** — Pulls a second leg out of an existing measuring line (protractor). The drag must start within 8 document pixels of either end (`RULER_ENDPOINT_HIT_RADIUS`), an app decision; Adobe states the gesture but not the radius. Without a radius, every Alt-drag anywhere would be a protractor.

**Shortcuts**

- `I` — Selects Eyedropper if no member of the Eyedropper/Color Sampler/Ruler group is selected; otherwise keeps the current group member.
- `Shift+I` — Cycles the tools that share the letter: Eyedropper, Color Sampler, Ruler, Note and Count. The app cycles its three implemented members (Eyedropper, Color Sampler and Ruler); Note and Count are absent.

**In this app:** `partial` — The tool is a pixel-free tool (`PIXEL_FREE_TOOLS`), so it has no entry in `toolProcessors.ts` and dispatches nothing — no history, no durable operation. Adobe calls the line "nonprinting" and gives its removals as drag-out or Clear, neither of which is an undo. Four behaviors diverge from Photoshop: (1) Protractor has one of Adobe's two gestures: Alt-drag is implemented; double-click-and-drag is not (Adobe does not specify which end pivots). (2) Measurement scale is missing with its `Image > Analysis` menu. (3) No Info panel; options bar is the only readout surface (Adobe names both). (4) Endpoint tolerance for protractor is 8 document pixels (`RULER_ENDPOINT_HIT_RADIUS`), an app decision; Adobe states the gesture but no radius. The line survives a tool switch and lives in a module store (`ruler-measurement-store.ts`), not `StoreContext`. The rule is drawn at 1 CSS px at every contain fit (`RULE_WIDTH_CSS`), dark edge then light face for contrast over any background. `isInsideFrame` uses `<=` on the frame bounds so a line exactly on the edge is kept.

### Draw Tool

`draw`

Photoshop's name for it is **No Photoshop tool — this app's own tool (nearest Photoshop: Brush tool)**.

This app's own freehand stroke tool (OVR-2 override): a drag becomes a new layer of ink, drawn with Pen, Dashed Pen, or Spray renderers.

Draw is the app-only OVR-2 override: Photoshop has no Draw tool, but this app deliberately keeps one. This bar documents its local behavior rather than claiming Photoshop parity. A drag accumulates pointer samples into a stroke; the stroke is drawn in the foreground color; the finished stroke is committed as a new layer (each mark is a separately undoable, separately deletable object). A Pen Type dropdown picks one of three renderers — Pen (solid round-capped stroke), Dashed Pen (dashed stroke with configurable Dash and Gap), Spray (soft radial gradients with Flow controlling deposit rate). Size, Opacity, and Spray Flow shape all three; Dash and Gap are Dashed Pen only. A live preview at the end of the bar draws the current settings. A user coming from Photoshop should reach for the Brush tool for the solid stroke. This app has no dedicated Airbrush toggle; Spray Flow builds deposits while the pointer is held. There is no Photoshop equivalent to a dashed freehand ink stroke. No keyboard shortcut is declared (OVR-2); the tool is reachable by pointer only.

**Options bar**

| Control             | Photoshop                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | In this app                                                  |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Brush Preset picker | Opens the brush tip chooser, and lets the current preset's Size and Hardness be changed without reopening the Brush panel. The app has no brush tips, so there is no picker and no hardness.                                                                         | `missing`                                                    |
| Size                | The diameter of the brush tip, in pixels. Photoshop's Size runs from 1 to 5000 px; the app's slider runs from 0.5 to 500 in steps of 0.5.                                                                                                                            | `partial` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Draw/Draw.tsx:172` |
| Mode                | The blend mode the stroke's paint composites with. Default: Normal. Declared on args but no Draw-bar control writes it; the value is always absent.                                                                                                                  | `missing`                                                    |
| Opacity             | The transparency of the color applied. As a stroke passes over an area the color does not exceed this level until the button is released; a further stroke adds more. Adobe states no default; the app seeds 90% for Pen and Dashed Pen, 50% for Spray.              | `partial` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Draw/Draw.tsx:234` |
| Flow                | The rate at which spray deposits build while the pointer is held, independently of Opacity. The app exposes a 1–100% Flow slider for Spray only; one tap remains visible at any Flow. Adobe states no default for it.                                                | `partial` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Draw/Draw.tsx:257` |
| Airbrush            | A toggle that keeps the brush laying down color while the pointer is held still. The Draw bar has no dedicated Airbrush toggle; its Spray Flow control does build deposits during a stationary hold, but Spray is selected from the Pen Type dropdown.               | `missing`                                                    |
| Smoothing           | How much intelligent smoothing is applied to the stroke, 0 to 100. Adobe names the Brush, Pencil, Mixer Brush and Eraser as the tools it applies to. The app declares `smoothing` on the draw args but no Draw-bar control writes it, so the value is always absent. | `missing`                                                    |
| Pen Type            | App-only dropdown with three renderers: Pen (solid round-capped), Dashed Pen (dashed with Dash/Gap), Spray (soft radial gradients). Not a Photoshop control.                                                                                                         | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Draw/Draw.tsx:140` |
| Dash                | Dashed Pen only: the length of each dash in pixels. No Photoshop counterpart.                                                                                                                                                                                        | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Draw/Draw.tsx:188` |
| Gap                 | Dashed Pen only: the gap between dashes in pixels. No Photoshop counterpart.                                                                                                                                                                                         | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Draw/Draw.tsx:201` |

**In this app:** `implemented` — No Photoshop provenance is claimed and none is invented: the Tools panel has no freehand-annotation or pen-stroke tool, and this app's Draw tile sits in the tonal group where Photoshop has no tool at all (OVR-2). The nearest Photoshop tools are the Pen tool family (path work) and the Brush (freehand paint). The `shortcut` field on a toolbar entry is display-only and binds nothing; its only consumers are the tile tooltip and the `<kbd>` in the flyout. Key bindings live in a separate hand-written table. This tool declares no shortcut. Adobe's published default-keyboard-shortcut reference gives no letter for a Draw tool, so there is no Adobe binding this app is surrendering; the letters are occupied by this app's own keymap — `W`/`Shift+W` select Object Selection, `B`/`Shift+B` select the Brush group — so there is no free key to declare. It was previously badged `B`, which was wrong twice: `B` belongs to the Brush in Photoshop, and in this app `B` is bound to the brush group with `Shift+B` cycling it, so pressing `B` selected the Brush and could never select this tool. The badge is gone rather than reassigned because a declared shortcut the app does not implement is a falsehood the rail prints. Photoshop's spring-loaded switch is also absent: no key selects this tool, so holding a letter cannot reach it either. The `Mode` and `Smoothing` fields are declared on args but unreachable from this bar — no draw control writes either, the default args set neither, and a draw stroke's layer is forced to Normal by the blend-mode gate that admits only the paint tools. Three of the Brush bar's controls diverge rather than match: Size capped at 500 vs 5000, Opacity seeded per-pen vs 100%, and no Flow on Pen/Dashed Pen (Spray Flow is a different control). Each stroke commits via `createLayerFromTool` (new layer), unlike Photoshop's Brush which paints into the active layer.

## View and navigation

Long-form research, provenance and unverified claims: [`src/tools/descriptions/view.notes.md`](../src/tools/descriptions/view.notes.md).

### Hand Tool

`hand` · **H**

Pans the canvas; double-click or Fit On Screen restores contain-fit. No flick momentum, Pan All Windows or Overscroll.

The Hand tool moves the viewport over an image that is larger than the window. It changes only the presentation of the canvas, so panning never creates a History entry or changes exported pixels. Hold Space while another non-Type tool is active for Photoshop's temporary Hand behavior. Double-clicking the Hand surface resets the view to the default centered contain-fit (Fit On Screen). The app also provides a 100% button that centers the image at one image pixel per physical display pixel, accounting for display density.

**Options bar**

| Control            | Photoshop                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | In this app                                                 |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Fit On Screen      | Restores the default centered view so the whole image fits the workspace (contain-fit). Implemented as a button that dispatches `DEFAULT_VIEW_STATE`.                                                                             | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/View/View.tsx:32` |
| 100%               | Returns the view to a centered 100% scale without rotating the document. At 100%, one image pixel maps to one monitor pixel (accounting for device pixel ratio). Implemented as a button that sets zoom to the 1:1 magnification. | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/View/View.tsx:38` |
| Zoom level display | The app adds a live percentage readout and +/- step buttons to the Hand bar; Photoshop places its zoom controls on the Zoom tool bar rather than this Hand-bar control.                                                           | `partial` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/View/View.tsx:77` |

**Modifiers**

- **Space** — Temporarily pans with the Hand tool while another non-Type tool is active (spring-loaded). Implemented globally in `AppKeyboardShortcuts.tsx`.

**Shortcuts**

- `H` — Selects the Hand tool.
- `Space (hold)` — Spring-loaded Hand tool from any non-Type tool. Implemented globally.
- `Double-click` — Resets view to Fit On Screen (contain-fit). Implemented on the Hand surface.

**In this app:** `implemented` — Panning is transient and is not sent through the processor or history paths. The view state (`panX`, `panY`, `zoom`, `rotation`, `fitScaleCompensation`, `minimumZoomOverride`) lives in `StoreContext` and is updated directly by the tool area and options bar. Flick momentum, Pan All Windows, and the Overscroll preference are not implemented. The Hand bar includes zoom step buttons (+/-) and a live zoom readout that Photoshop's Hand bar does not have (Photoshop puts zoom controls on the Zoom tool's bar). The 100% button on the Hand bar centers at 1:1 magnification; the Fit On Screen button restores the contain-fit. The lower bound follows document size so the shorter edge reaches one physical display pixel — an aspect-ratio interpretation of Adobe's documented one-pixel minimum. Animated zoom, marquee zoom, and wheel preferences are not implemented.

### Rotate View Tool

`rotate-view`

Rotates the canvas view; Shift snaps to 15°. Esc, Reset View or double-click returns to 0°. No compass, GPU checks or Rotate All Windows.

The Rotate View tool turns the displayed canvas so a retoucher can work at a comfortable angle. The image data remains unchanged and the rotation is not recorded in History. Drag around the workspace centre to rotate; the rotation angle is measured from the viewport center. Press Escape or click Reset View to return to zero degrees. Double-click the tool surface also resets. The options bar provides a numeric angle input (-180 to 180) and a Reset View button.

**Options bar**

| Control        | Photoshop                                                                                                                                                                                    | In this app                                                  |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Rotation Angle | Sets the displayed angle from -180 to 180 degrees. A numeric input with `step="any"`. The value is normalized to (-180, 180] with -180 mapped to 180. Implemented in `RotateView` component. | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/View/View.tsx:185` |
| Reset View     | Returns the displayed rotation to zero without changing pixels. Implemented as a button that sets `rotation: 0`.                                                                             | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/View/View.tsx:195` |

**Modifiers**

- **Shift** — Snaps a rotate drag to 15° increments. Implemented: `event.shiftKey ? Math.round(rotation / 15) * 15 : rotation`.

**Shortcuts**

- `R` — Selects the Rotate View tool.
- `Shift+H` — Cycles between the Hand and Rotate View tools. Implemented in `AppKeyboardShortcuts.tsx`.
- `Esc` — Resets the view angle to zero while Rotate View is active. Implemented in `ViewToolArea` (double-click also resets).
- `Double-click` — Resets the view angle to zero. Implemented on the Rotate View surface.

**In this app:** `implemented` — Rotation is a CSS presentation transform (`transform: rotate(${rotation}deg)`) applied to the workspace canvas and remains outside document history. The rotation is measured from the viewport center, not the document center. The angle is normalized to the range (-180, 180] with -180 mapped to 180. Graphics-processor capability checks, a compass overlay, and Rotate All Windows are not implemented. The Shift constraint (15° increments) applies during the drag gesture, not to the numeric input. The tool surface cursor is `cursor-grab` when idle, `cursor-grabbing` when dragging.

Implementation:

- `src/components/Main/ViewToolArea.tsx:99`
- `src/components/ToolbarsRight/View/View.tsx:174`
- `src/components/Common/AppKeyboardShortcuts.tsx:502`

### Zoom Tool

`zoom` · **Z**

Click or scrub to zoom around the pointer; Ctrl/Cmd+wheel zooms and unmodified wheel pans. No animated or marquee zoom.

The Zoom tool changes the displayed scale of the canvas and keeps the clicked point under the pointer. Click to zoom in, hold Alt or Option to zoom out, and drag horizontally for a scrubby zoom. View scale is transient and never becomes a document edit or History entry. The options bar provides a continuous zoom slider (0–VIEW_ZOOM_SLIDER_STEPS), a live zoom readout, Fit On Screen, and 100% buttons. The lower bound follows document size so the shorter edge reaches one physical display pixel — an aspect-ratio interpretation of Adobe's documented one-pixel minimum.

**Options bar**

| Control       | Photoshop                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | In this app                                                  |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Zoom          | Continuous zoom slider ranging from the document minimum zoom (shorter edge = 1 physical pixel) up to 3200% (32x). The slider maps non-linearly to magnification via `viewZoomToSliderPosition` / `sliderPositionToViewZoom`. The readout shows the current percentage. Photoshop's bar has a similar slider and a text field for typing an exact percentage. | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/View/View.tsx:136` |
| Fit On Screen | Resets the view to the centered contain-fit scale. Implemented as a button.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/View/View.tsx:32`  |
| 100%          | Centers the image at one image pixel per physical display pixel, accounting for display density. Implemented as a button.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/View/View.tsx:38`  |

**Modifiers**

- **Alt/Option** — Reverses a click or scrubby drag from zoom-in to zoom-out. Implemented: `alternate` flag on gesture reads `event.altKey`.
- **Ctrl/Cmd + wheel** — Zooms around the cursor. Implemented in `onWheel` handler.

**Shortcuts**

- `Z` — Selects the Zoom tool.
- `Click` — Zoom in (1.25x step) at the click point.
- `Alt/Option + Click` — Zoom out (0.8x step) at the click point.
- `Drag horizontally` — Scrubby zoom (continuous zoom proportional to drag distance).
- `Ctrl/Cmd + Wheel` — Zoom around cursor.
- `Wheel` — Pan (when Zoom tool is active and no modifier).

**In this app:** `implemented` — The view percentage stays stable when the workspace is resized or moved between displays with different pixel density; pan and zoom remain outside document history. The zoom slider uses a non-linear mapping to magnification (`VIEW_ZOOM_SLIDER_STEPS` = 1000 steps) with a dynamic minimum zoom that ensures the shorter document edge reaches at least one physical display pixel. The slider interaction freezes the minimum zoom floor (`interactionMinimumZoom`) during drag/keyboard interaction so the slider doesn't jump when the floor changes. The minimum zoom floor is derived from `minimumSliderZoomForCurrentView` which accounts for document frame size, current magnification, and any `minimumZoomOverride` from prior crops. Animated zoom, marquee zoom (drag a box to zoom to it), and wheel preferences (zoom on scroll without modifier) are not implemented. Double-click on the Zoom surface does not reset (only Hand and Rotate View do).

## Patch

Long-form research, provenance and unverified claims: [`src/tools/descriptions/patch.notes.md`](../src/tools/descriptions/patch.notes.md).

### Patch Tool

`patch`

Repairs a selection with texture dragged from a donor. This app implements Source only; Destination, Content-Aware, Pattern and Transparent are unavailable.

Photoshop's Patch Tool uses an active selection as the repair target in Source mode, then samples a donor area while the selection is dragged. The donor texture is blended into the target with luminance matching so the repair does not change the target area's overall brightness. Diffusion controls the feather width at the patch boundary (1–7, mapping to a 0–1 feather factor). This app implements a deterministic MVP: an existing active selection, Source mode only, a donor drag, and a replayable raster action. Content-Aware, Destination, Pattern, and Transparent modes are deferred because their synthesis is proprietary or requires architecture not present.

**Options bar**

| Control                        | Photoshop                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | In this app                                                   |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Patch                          | Mode selector: Source (drag the selection to a donor area) or Destination (drag a donor area into the selection). The app renders a disabled dropdown showing only Source; Destination is not implemented. Photoshop also offers Content-Aware, Pattern, and Transparent modes in this dropdown.                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `partial` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Patch/Patch.tsx:15` |
| Diffusion                      | Controls the deterministic edge feather approximation from 1 to 7. The app maps this to a feather factor of `diffusion / 7` (0 to 1), applied as a linear falloff from the patch edge inward over 4 pixels: `weight = 1 - feather * min(1, min(distToLeft, distToTop, distToRight, distToBottom) / 4)`. Photoshop's Diffusion is described as "how quickly the pasted region adapts to the surrounding image" but the exact algorithm is not published; this app's linear falloff is an approximation. | `present` — `src/components/ToolbarsRight/Patch/Patch.tsx:19` |
| Structure / Color / Adaptation | Content-Aware controls. Structure (1–7) controls how closely the patch adheres to existing image structures; Color (0–10) controls color blending; Adaptation (Strict / Medium / Loose / Very Loose) controls how loosely the patch adapts. These are deferred because their synthesis is proprietary.                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `missing`                                                     |
| Sample All Layers              | When on, the donor is sampled from the merged visible layers rather than the active layer alone. The MVP samples and writes the active raster layer only.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `missing`                                                     |

**Modifiers**

- **Alt/Option** — Polygonal selection modifiers remain owned by the active selection tool. The Patch tool itself reads no modifier keys; it requires a pre-existing selection.

**Shortcuts**

- `J` — Selects the healing-tool flyout family; this app selects Healing Brush directly and exposes Patch from its flyout. Photoshop's J cycles Spot Healing Brush, Healing Brush, Patch, Red Eye, Remove, and Content-Aware Move.

**In this app:** `partial` — The tool requires an active selection (`activeSelectionId` with `isActive: true`) and a non-bedrock active layer. The selected target rectangle is preserved when switching into Patch and is cleared normally when leaving the tool. The processor stores rectangle and donor coordinates directly in the tool args so replay does not depend on live selection state. The gesture: pointer-down on the selection starts a drag; pointer-move previews the donor texture via `tempUpdateLayer` (live preview, no history); pointer-up commits via `updateLayerByTool` (one history entry). The donor point is computed as `selection.pos + (currentPointer - dragStart)`. Luminance correction matches the donor's luminance to the target before blending (`correction = targetLuminance - donorLuminance`), keeping the repaired patch from changing the target area's overall brightness. The feather factor is `diffusion / 7` (0 at diffusion=0, 1 at diffusion=7), applied as a linear falloff from the patch edge inward over 4 pixels. The blend uses `blendPixel` with the corrected donor color and the computed weight. The tool is disabled (cursor-not-allowed) when no valid selection or layer exists. No keyboard shortcut selects Patch directly; it is reached via the healing flyout from Healing Brush (J). Source mode only; Destination mode dropdown is rendered but disabled. Content-Aware, Pattern, and Transparent modes are absent. Sample All Layers is absent. The app has no Info panel readout for the patch.
